mathematical_summary: For a same-sign orthonormal spectral pair, the partner Pluecker determinant weights have exact incidence marginals equal to row leverage. Geometric Brascamp--Lieb with those leverage exponents and sharp Hausdorff--Young yields a universal e bound for the two-dimensional spectral projection, including a separate heavy-coordinate branch. Exact ellipse-shell area then gives density <= pi e/sqrt(|lambda1 lambda2|) for the pure rotated same-sign rank-two spectral quadratic component.
next_step: Retain the Pluecker weights inside the full small-ball/coarea trace and prove that a spectrally orthogonal remainder carrying the third large eigenvalue cannot correlate with the ellipse shell strongly enough to destroy the universal bound.
